title: Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue: whether Complaint 2015-12 was properly before the SJC. Held no; the complaint was administratively out of order. No merits ruling on Metro Atlanta Presbytery's June 29, 2015 dissolution of Grace North Atlanta. If pursued, the complaint must be filed with Presbytery within 30 days from notification of the SJC decision (OMSJC 9.2(c)).
first_summary: Wills complained to the SJC after Metro Atlanta Presbytery declared administratively out of order his earlier complaint against Grace North Atlanta's dissolution because it lacked a signature. The SJC held the complaint was not properly before it and was administratively out of order: BCO 43-2 required the complaint first be filed with Presbytery, which had not yet responded to the September 15 ruling. Wills could file with Presbytery within 30 days.
summary: After Metro Atlanta Presbytery dissolved Grace North Atlanta, a complaint challenging that action was declared administratively out of order for lacking a signature. Wills then complained to the SJC. The SJC held the SJC complaint was not properly before it and was administratively out of order: under BCO 43-2, a complaint must first go to the court whose act is challenged, and Presbytery had not yet addressed that ruling. Wills could file with Presbytery within 30 days. No merits ruling on the dissolution.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–3, 13–17, 50–52 (printed pp. 554–555): SJC Decision on Complaint March 3, 2016; opinion drafted by RE Nusbaum, edited by the Panel, and amended and approved by the SJC on roll-call vote.
evidence_notes.dispute: Source lines 21–27 (printed p. 554): Metro Atlanta Presbytery dissolved Grace North Atlanta on 6/29/15; Weekly, Flesher, and Wills complained on 7/16/15; MAP declared that complaint administratively out of order for lack of signature on 9/15/15; Wills filed the SJC complaint on 9/18/15.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Source lines 31–48 (printed p. 555): issue is whether Complaint 2015-12 is properly before the SJC; judgment “No. The Complaint is Administratively Out of Order”; BCO 43-2 requires a complaint first to the court whose act is alleged as error; MAP had no opportunity to respond to its 9/15/15 action; complainant may file with MAP within 30 days per OMSJC 9.2(c).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Source lines 50–52 (printed p. 555) show concurrences and dissents but no separate opinion text; lines 56–58 and 159–163 are proposed OMSJC amendments and officer elections, not merits rulings. The underlying dissolution was not decided.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated judicial decision; the source cites BCO 43-2 and OMSJC 9.2(c), not an adopted case result.
